$comment: Single source of truth for docs/pipeline-explorer.html and the Mermaid spine (scripts/docs/build-explorer.mjs). It models what the runner's rules say will happen for a configuration; it does not run anything. Settings name their real config path or CLI flag and say where the code keeps their default and allowed values (`checks`, verified by scripts/docs/test/pipeline-flow.test.mjs). Conditions are data: {"eq":[ref,value]}, {"in":[ref,[values]]}, {"is":ref}, {"not":c}, {"all":[c]}, {"any":[c]}, {"gt":[ref,n]}; a ref is a setting id or a fact id. A fact with "walk": true starts false and is set by the edges the walk takes ({"set":{fact:true}}); an outcome with cyclesLeft or cyclesUsed (a setting id) is offered only before, or once, that many visits of its step. Doc links are relative to docs/.

agent.label: Agent
agent.help: A fresh headless agent process (a model call).

harness.label: Harness
harness.help: Deterministic runner code: no agent, no model call (unless it says it calls one).

service.label: Outside service
service.help: Reached through a pluggable adapter (code host, tracker, CI system).

record.label: Record
record.help: What the run writes and reports.

exit.label: Exit
exit.help: The run stops here for this ticket; a person decides what happens next.

settings.label: Entry
settings.help: How the run starts. A bug epic is an epic whose tickets are strictly more than half bugs.

settings.label: Ticket kind
settings.help: A bug is a ticket of type bug (or a BUG-n key). A UI bug's verified plan has a browser case a changed spec runs; a backend bug's reproduction case drives the service through its public interface.

settings.label: The change touches
settings.help: Decided by the project model (project.frontendPaths, service kinds, prVideo.backendPaths). Frontend gets the demo video; any backend change gets the API changes section, mixed changes included.

settings.label: --pr (open a PR)
settings.help: Without --pr a run stops after the tests are verified: no push, no PR. The presets turn it on because the generated pipeline is run with it.

settings.label: Triage severity (bug PR)
settings.help: What the harness computes from the bug-triage agent's ratings and the floor rules. Only bug-fix PRs are rated.

settings.label: Triage confidence
settings.help: High when every ticket's confidence is at least implement.reviewGate.confidence.highMin (85) with no owner question.

settings.label: Delivery
settings.help: story: every ticket of an epic gets its own branch and PR, with no epic plan.

settings.label: Grouping
settings.help: Precedence: an explicit grouping wins (epic: one PR; ticket: one PR per ticket, no planner), then a strict bug majority (bug groups), then the PR split.

settings.label: PR split (feature epic)
settings.help: epic: one PR; story: one PR per story; groups: PRs of stories the orchestrator groups. Applies only when the epic is not mostly bugs and grouping is auto.

settings.label: Unit feature verification
settings.help: The cross-story journeys of an epic unit are planned, automated and verified once on the unit.

settings.label: Unit PR check
settings.help: The PR check of every ticket of a unit against the unit's diff, in one run.

settings.label: pairVerify
settings.help: Seat a council instead of the single pair-verifier.

settings.label: pairUiVerify
settings.help: Seat a council instead of the single pair-ui-verifier (UI subtasks).

settings.label: review
settings.help: Seat a council instead of the single architecture-reviewer.

settings.label: testPlan
settings.help: Seat a council instead of the single test-plan-verifier.

settings.label: testAutomation
settings.help: Seat a council instead of the single test-automation-verifier.

settings.label: prCheck
settings.help: Seat council members instead of the PR check critics.

settings.label: intercom (discussion)
settings.help: After a seated council's independent first round, its members discuss in a chat room before the merge: points settle by majority, a split goes to the stage's model or the owner. Off by default.

settings.label: intercom onSplit
settings.help: Who settles a split: the stage's orchestrating or judging model (implement, PR check; elsewhere the owner), or always the owner.

settings.label: intercom maxTurnsPerMember
settings.help: Posts per member in a discussion, and the number of discussion waves; disputes and votes are capped at twice this.

settings.label: Static analysis
settings.help: On when .factory/config.json has an analysis section. Off: no local analysis slots, and no analysis jobs are rendered for CI, so the pre-push analysis gate has nothing to run.

settings.label: Analysis fix loop
settings.help: Blocking analysis findings go back to the implementer this many times, without spending a review round.

settings.label: Demo video (features.demoVideo)
settings.help: Demo videos, bug before/after evidence and the API changes section, produced on the pipeline machine before the PR opens.

settings.label: Narration scope
settings.help: Which videos the demo-narrator agent scripts. none: automatic lines only, no narrator agent. Any other value stops every command that loads the pipeline config.

settings.label: Require before-the-fix evidence
settings.help: A bug whose reproduction cannot be shown before the fix (UI video pair or backend request evidence) opens no PR.

settings.label: maxPairRounds
settings.help: Rounds a pair gets before it escalates to the orchestrator (rewrite or takeover, once).

settings.label: review.maxRounds
settings.help: Architecture review rounds before the review escalates.

settings.label: maxBugFixCycles
settings.help: Times a product bug found by the automated tests goes back to implementation.

settings.label: Return PR check findings to implementation
settings.help: Off: every PR check finding stays with pr-check-fixer.

settings.label: returnToImplementation.maxReturns
settings.help: Returns from the PR check to implementation or test automation per ticket (a wrongly routed one is re-routed once for free).

settings.label: returnToImplementation.minSeverity
settings.help: The least severe production finding that returns; below it pr-check-fixer handles it.

settings.label: ciFixRounds
settings.help: 0 sends red CI straight to a person. Any value above 0 gives one fixing round per CI gate (the gate runs at most one).

settings.label: preOpen.draftCycles
settings.help: Times an open PR may go back on hold for a CI fixing round before a person decides.

settings.label: preOpen.afterOpen (hold mode)
settings.help: How an open PR is held while agents work on it again. close-reopen becomes draft on a host that cannot reopen (Bitbucket), with a warning when implement, the review gate or factory doctor load the config. Another value stops the config from loading.

settings.label: ciWait
settings.help: false: no CI proof on the branch before the open and no wait for the PR's checks after it (the PR opens without the proof).

settings.label: autoMerge.enabled
settings.help: The kill switch: off, every PR that would auto-merge waits for approvals instead.

settings.label: approvals.Low
settings.help: Approvals a Low PR needs when it does not auto-merge.

settings.label: approvals.Medium
settings.help: Approvals a Medium PR needs.

settings.label: approvals.High
settings.help: Approvals a High PR needs.

settings.label: approvals.Severe
settings.help: Approvals a Severe PR needs.

settings.label: Code host
settings.help: Detected from the origin remote; github without one.

settings.label: Tracker (board)
settings.help: The host's own tracker by default (Bitbucket has none: set it).

settings.label: CI system
settings.help: The host's own CI system by default. Whether it runs pipelines on a branch push (capability branchPipelines) decides between proving CI before the open and opening as a draft.

settings.label: custom CI declares branchPipelines
settings.help: A custom CI adapter's capabilities come from its describe operation and ci.capabilities.

branchPipelines.$comment: The CI adapters' capability branchPipelines (scripts/pipeline/lib/ci/<provider>.mjs CAPABILITIES); custom: declared.

normalize.note: A feature epic's tickets are stories: ticket kind is feature.
A bug epic's tickets are bugs: ticket kind set to UI bug.
A UI bug's fix touches the frontend: change set to frontend and backend.

facts.label: an epic run was asked for
a ticket delivers its own PR
one epic branch and one PR
a feature epic split into PRs
bug groups (strict bug majority, or grouping ticket)
the PR is a bug-fix PR (rated by the gate)
the CI system runs pipelines on a branch push
CI is proven on the branch before the open
the PR opens as a draft (or labelled) and is marked ready when green
the PR is already open with a hold recorded (a re-delivery, or a resumed wait): it is updated, not opened, and released when green
demo video of the changed specs
the ticket's own PR check is waited for
PR check findings can return to implementation
red CI gets a fixing round
a failing check after the open gets a hold and a fixing round
a model rules on a split

nodes.label: Start the run
nodes.desc: implement run (a ticket, or --epic for every ticket of an epic) refuses to start while another run is active here, recovers a dead run's daemons, fetches the tickets and plans the batch in Blocked-by order.

nodes.label: implement resume / requeue
nodes.desc: Continues a run that stopped, from its saved phase, or (requeue) runs again a ticket a person resolved or reopened. A PR that did not open (pr-refused, gate-assessment-failed), or a held PR whose rating failed, replays the delivery from the analysis gate and push, even under needs-human, while the branch is at the head CI proved; a rating or demo media saved for that head is reused. A stopped CI wait resumes there; when a hold is still recorded (hold-failed, release-unconfirmed, a held or draft PR) it is released once green, with the CI wait off too.

nodes.label: Sync the board, claim the card
nodes.desc: board sync, then the claim moves the card to In Progress from Backlog, Ready, Failed or In Progress (Pending Review and Done only with --force); a card another machine holds is skipped unless --takeover.

nodes.label: One ticket or an epic?
nodes.desc: A ticket delivers its own PR; an epic run (implement.delivery epic) is delivered in units. --delivery story runs an epic's tickets one PR each, with no epic plan.

nodes.label: Hold the open PR
nodes.desc: After the claim, with --pr, a ticket whose PR is still open (reopened, sent back, or its last record names an open or unreadable PR: one host read at plan time, after the skip, resume and reopen routing, none under --dry-run) runs on that PR's branch: the PR is put on hold (preOpen.afterOpen) and the hold confirmed before any agent runs; a hold already confirmed is kept. The reopened label stays until then. Without --pr nothing is held. After a merge it becomes a follow-up branch and a new PR instead.

nodes.label: A person resolves or reopens it
nodes.desc: The person answers the questions on the Failed ticket and ticks Resolved, or reopens a delivered bug fix (or sends its PR back); board sync moves it to Ready and implement requeue (or run) claims it again, with the answers as binding decisions.

nodes.label: Tracker
nodes.desc: The ticket board, through the tracker adapter: lanes, ticket text, evidence, questions.

nodes.label: Epic plan
nodes.desc: The orchestrator writes the epic's design note (contracts, journeys) and, for planned groups, the PR groups the harness validates; grouping ticket skips it.

nodes.label: Delivery units
nodes.desc: The units the epic is delivered in: one epic branch, or PR groups (one per story, planned groups, or bug groups) stacked on the groups they depend on.

nodes.label: Foundation pair
nodes.desc: When the design note names a foundation (shared contracts), one pair builds it on the epic branch before the stories.

nodes.label: Orchestrator plans
nodes.desc: Keeps the ticket (self mode) or plans up to implement.maxSubtasks subtasks with owned files; the harness validates the plan. In an epic this runs for every ticket of the unit.

nodes.label: Implementer
nodes.desc: A pair-implementer writes each subtask in its own worktree (the orchestrator itself in self mode); review fixes, product bugs and PR check returns come back here.

nodes.label: Harness checks
nodes.desc: After every implementer run: language-server errors, whitespace-only hunks, the repository's lint on changed lines and, with static analysis on, the analysis tools; a secret only in unpushed commits is folded out by the harness.

nodes.label: Pair verifier
nodes.desc: A fresh read-only verifier (pair-ui-verifier on a test-stack slot for UI subtasks) or a council checks each round; approved subtasks are merged into the story branch.

nodes.label: Policy engine
nodes.desc: The architecture policy engine runs first, deterministically; a block goes back to the implementer.

nodes.label: Architecture review
nodes.desc: A fresh architecture-reviewer (or a council) approves the code on disk; approval moves the card to Testing.

nodes.label: Test plan
nodes.desc: Feature verification workflow 1: the test plan, checked by test-plan-verifier (or a council); required cases from the PR check or the pairs are added.

nodes.label: Test automation
nodes.desc: Workflow 2: automated tests for every case, checked by test-automation-verifier (or a council); a test that finds a product bug sends the change back.

nodes.label: Merged into the unit branch
nodes.desc: Each verified ticket merges into its unit's branch (the epic branch or its group branch); the per-ticket PR check is skipped in units.

nodes.label: Run ends: done, no PR
nodes.desc: Without --pr: outcome done, the ticket published, the card to Pending Review with its evidence; the branch stays local (an epic unit stays merged on its branch).

nodes.label: Unit feature verification
nodes.desc: The cross-story journeys, verified once per unit (a split feature epic: on the last journey group, stacked on the others; a bug group: only journeys wholly inside it); tests later tickets made stale are re-verified.

nodes.label: Unit PR check
nodes.desc: Every ticket of the unit checked against the unit's diff in one run; fix mode lets pr-check-fixer fix upheld findings, and an escalated check stops the unit after the push.

nodes.label: Council discussion
agents: implement orchestrator or PR check judge (splits)
nodes.desc: With a stage's council seated and council.intercom on: after the members' independent first round, they discuss in a chat room (at most {council.intercom.maxTurnsPerMember} posts each), only once and only when there is something to discuss. A point settles by a majority of all seats; a split goes to the stage's model or the owner; a product question goes to the owner. The stage then merges and decides as usual.

nodes.label: Back to the stage
nodes.desc: The stage merges round 1 with the discussion's result: withdrawn, dropped and noted findings become notes, revised scores count, and it decides as its own step shows.

nodes.label: PR check
nodes.desc: Critics (or council members), a defender and a judge debate the change against its ticket; the harness computes the score and routes each upheld finding by what would resolve it. Not waited for when the Stop hook's check is off (prCheck.hook.enabled false, or PR_CHECK_SKIP=1): delivery goes straight on.

nodes.label: pr-check-fixer
nodes.desc: Fixes findings confined to tests, docs, records, PR text or style, and production findings below minSeverity (implement.prCheck.fixUntil, bugFixUntil).

nodes.label: Publish, CI parity, re-verify
nodes.desc: A single ticket's or a bug group's tickets are published and fetched back as CI reads them (a feature epic's PRs read their own ticket copies), what CI runs on the PR runs here first (failures go through a fixing round), and another ticket's verified plan or tests this change edited is verified again. Every PR gets it: a single ticket, a bug group (also when a reopened ticket joins its open PR), a feature epic as one PR and each PR of a split epic. A check that still fails after one fixing run is reported in the PR body; it does not stop the delivery. implement.ciParity false skips the parity run of a single ticket and of a feature epic's PRs (a bug group's still runs) and, for every delivery, the pre-push analysis gate.

nodes.label: Pre-push analysis gate
nodes.desc: CI's analysis jobs (rendered only with static analysis on) run with CI's own script on a clean checkout of the head before anything is pushed; a secret the commit gate held still in the worktree stops the push. implement.ciParity false skips the gate too.

nodes.label: Analysis fixing round
nodes.desc: One fixing round on the blocking findings; a secret only in unpushed commits is folded out by the harness.

nodes.label: Push the branch
nodes.desc: The branch is pushed once the records it carries are redacted and scanned; then the tickets are published.

nodes.label: Owner question or unfinished check?
nodes.desc: Checked after the push, before the CI proof: an owner question from the PR check, or a PR check that did not finish (or a unit check that escalated), opens no PR.

nodes.label: CI proven on the branch head
nodes.desc: Every pipeline a push of the branch runs must complete green on that exact SHA (a skipped run is not a pass, a retry-only pass is a finding); if the base moved it is merged in and the new head proven again.

nodes.label: CI fixing round
nodes.desc: One fixing round on the failing checks (the PR check in fix mode, pushed), then the harness's own way out once (CI's analysis jobs here, the secret decision table), then the head is proven again.

nodes.label: CI system
nodes.desc: The CI adapter reads the head's runs, statuses and logs.

nodes.label: A bug fix?
nodes.desc: A bug ticket (type bug or a BUG-n key), or a bug group of a bug epic, is rated by the review gate; a feature PR, a feature epic or its groups are not.

nodes.label: Bug triage
nodes.desc: The read-only bug-triage agent rates each bug ticket (Impact, Complexity, Fix risk) from the branch's change; the harness computes Severity and Confidence. A resumed delivery reuses a saved rating. If the active gate cannot assess, no new PR opens. With the review gate off (implement.reviewGate.enabled false, or REVIEW_GATE=0) nothing is rated or published.

nodes.label: Static analysis of the head
nodes.desc: The delivered head's own scan for the PR body (deterministic; a head already scanned is not scanned again).

nodes.label: Demo video
nodes.desc: The changed e2e specs recorded in demo mode on a test-stack slot of this machine, narrated (demo-narrator, by narration scope) and subtitled, checked for secrets and stored for this head; a failed step is a note, never a hold.

nodes.label: UI bug: before / after videos
nodes.desc: The bug's reproducing browser case recorded against the merge base (it must fail at its check) and on the fix (it passes), narrated as a pair.

nodes.label: Backend bug: request evidence
nodes.desc: The reproduction case's requests and responses recorded on the base and on the fix: only a Playwright assertion that fails after the block's first recorded response counts. A Reproduction comment on the ticket (one not posted is a minor finding and a note in the PR) and a Before / After section in the PR (a backend-only change films nothing). Card fields and numbers are masked in this evidence only, by JSON key, form key and check digit.

nodes.label: API changes section
nodes.desc: One entry per HTTP endpoint added, changed or removed (route extractor or OpenAPI diff), with example calls the specs recorded; any change with backend code gets it, mixed frontend and backend included.

nodes.label: Open the PR, or update the held one
nodes.desc: The body is written whole and the PR opens once on the proven head (deliverFinished); on a CI system without branch pipelines it opens as a draft, confirmed by re-reading the PR, with the work-in-progress label as fallback. A PR already open and held (a re-delivery) gets its body refreshed instead: the same PR, never a second one.

nodes.label: Code host
nodes.desc: The host adapter pushes, opens, holds and merges PRs.

nodes.label: Gate publishes the rating
nodes.desc: The saved rating is published on the PR, the tickets and the board with --no-agent: no model call. An unreadable rating is published as not assessed (review, needs-human). A feature PR gets no rating. Skipped when the review gate is off.

nodes.label: Wait for the PR's checks
nodes.desc: The PR's own checks are waited for with no fixing agent; a check only a PR runs, or a moved base, can still fail here. With implement.ciWait false nothing is waited for and the run goes on as green.

nodes.label: Hold the PR
nodes.desc: The PR goes back to draft, gets the work-in-progress label, or is closed (preOpen.afterOpen) before any agent works on it again; Bitbucket cannot reopen, so close-reopen becomes draft there. The hold is confirmed by re-reading the PR (up to 3 reads, 1 s apart); a hold that is not confirmed stops the run before any agent. A PR already confirmed on hold (draft-first, a re-delivery) keeps its hold.

nodes.label: CI fixing round on hold
nodes.desc: One fixing round on the branch while the PR is held; still failing with cycles left, another round on the same hold, at most preOpen.draftCycles rounds in all.

nodes.label: Release the hold, mark ready
nodes.desc: Every hold not yet released (a draft-first open, a re-delivered or resumed PR, a fixing round) is released only when every expected check is green on the head, with the CI wait off too, each release confirmed by re-reading the PR; the run records ready only when all are confirmed.

nodes.label: Run ends: outcome done
nodes.desc: The run reports done with the PR open; the card stays in Pending Review. Run outcome done is not the board's Done lane, which needs the merge.

nodes.label: Review gate decides
nodes.desc: At the open and at every board sync. A bug PR auto-merges only when: every ticket assessed and Low, high confidence, no owner question, no human reopen (each ticket's history and every PR it was delivered in read at that moment; unreadable history needs a person), no delivery waiting for a person, the PR itself Low (no floor or bump), checks green, not already sent to people, unchanged since assessed, the delivery check ran on this head, and autoMerge.enabled. Otherwise approvals:N and needs-human. A feature PR waits under the host's own rules. With the review gate off, nothing is rated or auto-merged and the PR waits under the host's rules.

nodes.label: Auto-merge
nodes.desc: Merged through the host adapter, bound to the head the gate assessed (where the host can; Bitbucket re-reads the head before merging).

nodes.label: A person reviews
nodes.desc: Approvals counted by the review-quorum check on the latest push (bug PRs), or the repository's own branch rules (feature PRs).

nodes.label: Merged: card to Done
nodes.desc: The issues close with the merge and board sync moves the cards to the Done lane.

nodes.label: Sent back: reopen recorded
nodes.desc: board sync records a human reopen (changes requested, the PR closed without merge, card moved back, issue reopened; implement requeue after a person's decision on a delivered PR): severity rises, every later delivery of the ticket needs a person, and requeue or a run starts the ticket again.

nodes.label: Skipped

remains.ticket: the card where it was (another machine holds it, it waits for a person, or it is already implemented)

nodes.continue: --takeover for a card another machine holds, --force for an implemented ticket; a ticket waiting for a person runs once it is resolved.
nodes.desc: The claim is refused or the ticket is skipped.

nodes.label: Epic plan failed

remains.branch: the epic branch with whatever the foundation committed
remains.ticket: every ticket blocked by the epic plan, with the findings

nodes.continue: A person fixes the epic or its tickets; implement resume continues the saved epic state.
nodes.desc: The epic plan or its foundation failed: no ticket runs.

nodes.label: Escalation: implementation

remains.branch: the story branch in its worktree, not pushed
remains.ticket: the findings and up to three questions from the escalation-questions agent; card in Failed

nodes.epic: In an epic the unit gets no PR, tickets that depend on it are skipped, and independent units go on.
nodes.continue: Answer the questions on the ticket and tick Resolved; board sync moves it to Ready and implement requeue (or run <KEY>) runs it with the decisions.
nodes.desc: Planning or a pair could not finish.

nodes.label: Review escalated

remains.branch: the story branch, not pushed; the escalation note in the worktree
remains.ticket: the blocking findings and questions; card in Failed

nodes.epic: In an epic the unit gets no PR; dependents are skipped.
nodes.continue: Answer on the ticket and tick Resolved (or delete the escalation note after fixing by hand); requeue or run it again.
nodes.desc: The review did not approve within its rounds, or the implementer runs ran out.

nodes.label: Feature verification failed

remains.branch: the story branch with the plan and tests so far (not verified), not pushed
remains.ticket: the bugs or the escalation; card in Failed

nodes.epic: In an epic the unit gets no PR; dependents are skipped.
nodes.continue: Answer on the ticket and Resolve; crashed and timed-out runs resume with implement resume.
nodes.desc: The plan or tests did not verify, or product bugs remained after the bug-fix cycles.

nodes.label: Unit gets no PR

remains.branch: the unit branch with the tickets merged so far
remains.ticket: the failed tickets in Failed; the epic's evidence comment
remains.pr: none for this unit; an already open group PR stays on hold

nodes.continue: Resolve the failed tickets; implement resume (or the epic run again) continues the unit and skips units already delivered.
nodes.desc: A ticket of the unit, the unit's journeys or a stale-test re-verification failed.

nodes.label: Unresolved after returns

remains.branch: the story branch with the verified tests committed, not pushed
remains.ticket: the findings still upheld (or returned with nothing addressed); card in Failed

nodes.continue: Answer on the ticket and Resolve; requeue runs it with the decision.
nodes.desc: The PR check still upholds findings after maxReturns returns, or a return came back with nothing addressed.

nodes.label: Not delivered

remains.branch: pushed if the push got that far
remains.pr: none (an open PR on hold stays on hold)

nodes.continue: Fix the cause (another ticket's tests, the push, the base merge) and run the ticket again.
nodes.desc: Re-verifying another ticket's tests failed, the push or base sync failed, or the open failed for a reason other than the text.

nodes.label: Blocked before the push

remains.ticket: the analysis findings or the held secret's location (never its value); card in Failed

nodes.continue: Remove the secret or fix the finding in the worktree, then run the ticket again.
nodes.desc: CI's analysis jobs still fail after the fixing round, or a held secret is still in the worktree.

nodes.label: needs-decision

remains.ticket: published, the owner's question asked on it; card in Failed
remains.pr: none (an open PR on hold stays on hold)

nodes.continue: The owner answers on the ticket and ticks Resolved; requeue runs it with the decision.
nodes.desc: The PR check raised a question only the ticket's owner can answer.

nodes.label: PR check incomplete
nodes.continue: Resolve on the ticket; requeue or run again.
nodes.desc: The PR check did not finish, or a unit's check ended escalated or with findings at fixUntil or worse.

nodes.label: CI not green: no PR

remains.ticket: the failing checks and what the fix round did; card in Failed

nodes.continue: A person decides from the ticket's questions; requeue or run again after the fix.
nodes.desc: CI on the branch head is red, passed only with retries, cannot be read, conflicts, or the fix round escalated.

nodes.label: demo-video-blocked

remains.ticket: why the bug could not be shown before the fix (DEMO-NO-REPRO / API-NO-REPRO); card in Failed

nodes.continue: Fix the reproduction case (or turn requireBefore off) and run the ticket again.
nodes.desc: requireBefore is on and the UI video pair or the backend request evidence could not show the bug on the base.

nodes.label: gate-assessment-failed

remains.branch: pushed; CI-proven unless the proof was bypassed (draft-first or ciWait off)
remains.ticket: the finding GATE-ASSESS-FAILED; card in Failed
remains.pr: no new PR; a re-delivered PR stays open on hold

nodes.continue: Fix the gate CLI or the triage agent (or turn the gate off). A PR that never opened: the next run or implement resume replays the delivery from the analysis gate and push, even under needs-human, and rates again before the open. A held re-delivery resumes at the rating too, on hold, and then updates the same PR; no agent stage runs again unless the branch moved since CI proved it.
nodes.desc: The review gate is on and could not produce the bug-triage assessment before the open: no new PR opens. A re-delivered PR stays open on hold.

nodes.label: pr-refused

remains.pr: none; the title and body are saved

nodes.continue: implement resume runs the delivery again from the saved title and body: no implementation, review or test agent; the analysis gate, the CI proof, the demo-video step (narrator) and triage (when no rating was saved) can run again.
nodes.desc: The code host refused the PR's text even with the shortest body.

nodes.label: On hold: a person decides

remains.ticket: the CI findings; tickets in Failed
remains.pr: open; on hold when a hold was applied; the gate requires a person

nodes.continue: A person fixes it on the branch or decides; implement resume --stopped continues a stopped CI wait.
nodes.desc: A check failed after the open and no fixing round is left (every preOpen.draftCycles cycle used, or ciFixRounds 0), or CI could not be read or conflicts.

nodes.label: hold-failed

remains.ticket: the finding PR-HOLD-FAILED; card in Failed
remains.pr: open; it may already be in draft or labelled; no agent ran

nodes.continue: Check the PR on the host, then tick Resolved: after the open the run resumes at the CI wait; a reopened ticket keeps its reopened label and is held again first.
nodes.desc: The code host did not confirm the hold, so no agent works on the PR (also for a reopened ticket, an epic unit joined again, and a ticket whose last record left an open PR).

nodes.label: release-unconfirmed

remains.ticket: the finding PR-RELEASE-UNCONFIRMED; card in Failed
remains.pr: open, possibly still on hold; no ready time recorded

nodes.continue: Tick Resolved and the CI-wait resume releases every hold not yet released, or mark the PR ready by hand.
nodes.desc: Checks were green but the code host did not confirm releasing the PR from hold.

outcomes.label: a hold still recorded (hold-failed, release-unconfirmed, a held PR)
a person resolved it, no PR open
reopened or resolved, its PR still open
product bug found by a test
